_note: Scores are 0-100. trend_strength, visual_potential, originality and rendering_feasibility are human estimates made 2026-10-31 without YouTube API data; replace trend_strength with measured competitor view velocity once observations exist. novelty is computed by discovery/topics.py unless set here.

topics.title: What if Stanford was in Boston?

rationale.trend_strength: Stanford is widely recognized, but a plain relocation has a modest hook on its own.
rationale.visual_potential: Palm Drive, the Hoover Tower silhouette and a cross-country route read instantly; snow on the Main Quad is a strong reveal.
rationale.originality: No reference channel covers universities; relocation is the most common what-if shape, so not top marks.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Relocation is the weeks 1–4 build target and Patrick's V01 fixture already exists.

topics.title: What if Berkeley and Stanford switched campuses?

rationale.trend_strength: Big Game rivalry gives a built-in audience on both sides.
rationale.visual_potential: Two landmarks (Sather Tower, Hoover Tower) crossing paths on a map is a clear, symmetrical visual.
rationale.originality: Rivalry swaps are rare in what-if Shorts; the cultural clash angle is fresh.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Swap is scheduled for weeks 5–6 and reuses relocation routes.

topics.title: What if every public university disappeared?

rationale.trend_strength: Large stakes but abstract; needs a strong number in the first 3 seconds.
rationale.visual_potential: Dots vanishing across a national map is striking, though it lacks a close-up character beat by default.
rationale.originality: Nobody in the reference set does institution-scale disappearance.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: National map and filtering arrive in weeks 5–6; needs a pinned IPEDS cohort.

topics.title: What if Harvard moved to California?

rationale.trend_strength: Harvard is the most recognized university name globally.
rationale.visual_potential: Brick and ivy under palm trees is an immediate visual contrast.
rationale.originality: Similar shape to V01; publish them apart.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Reuses the V01 relocation system; needs a Harvard identity kit.

topics.title: What if MIT and Stanford swapped locations?

rationale.trend_strength: Tech-rivalry framing works, but it is a second Stanford swap.
rationale.visual_potential: The MIT Great Dome is a strong silhouette; fewer new visuals than V02.
rationale.originality: Overlaps V02's format; consider spacing them several weeks apart.

topics.title: What if every Ivy League university became public?

rationale.trend_strength: Admissions and tuition debates draw strong comment activity.
rationale.visual_potential: Status change is abstract; it needs gates opening, crowds, or acceptance-rate counters to read visually.
rationale.originality: Policy-flavoured hypotheticals are uncommon in the reference channels.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Status transformations land in weeks 7–8. Must not equate public status with free tuition.

topics.title: What if UCLA became the number-one university?

rationale.trend_strength: Rankings content performs, but a single-school premise mostly appeals to one fan base.
rationale.visual_potential: A leaderboard reorder is clear but static compared with map moves.
rationale.originality: Ranking videos are common in college content; hypothetical-rank framing helps a little.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Ranking reorder lands in weeks 7–8; label as hypothetical.

topics.title: What if every university became a country?

rationale.trend_strength: Map-and-flag what-ifs are a proven Shorts format.
rationale.visual_potential: Borders, flags and territory are highly visual and readable muted.
rationale.originality: Close to the common 'what if every state was a country' format, so lower originality.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Fictional borders for many institutions need grouping and instancing; weeks 7–8.

rationale.trend_strength: The Silicon Valley angle broadens the audience beyond college fans.
rationale.visual_potential: Absence is hard to show; needs before/after valley comparisons.
rationale.originality: Alternate-history framing is common in the references, but not for a university.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Absence and alternate-history comparison is a weeks 7–8 build. Use conditional language.

topics.title: What if all colleges merged into one campus?

rationale.trend_strength: Fun premise, but no single fan base to rally.
rationale.visual_potential: A giant generated master campus is a memorable final reveal.
rationale.originality: Nothing similar in the reference set.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Generated master layout is one of the last systems (weeks 9–10).

topics.title: What if every student transferred to Harvard?

rationale.trend_strength: Absurd-scale premise is shareable; Harvard name helps.
rationale.visual_potential: Crowd streams converging on Cambridge with a capacity counter is very visual.
rationale.originality: Scale-comparison hooks are common, but not applied to colleges.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Crowd flow and capacity comparison arrive weeks 9–10; keep illustrative crowd counts labelled.

rationale.trend_strength: Battle-royale and elimination formats perform strongly with younger audiences.
rationale.visual_potential: Shrinking territory and eliminations are the most kinetic idea on the list.
rationale.originality: Map-elimination formats are widespread, so originality depends on the university twist.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Needs territory, elimination states and rivalry systems; the last family built (weeks 9–10).

topics.title: What if Cal and Stanford traded campuses?
What if UC Berkeley moved to Texas?

rationale.visual_potential: Sather Tower in desert scrub is a clear contrast.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Reuses the V01 relocation system and the V02 Berkeley kit.

topics.title: What if Stanford moved to Cambridge, Massachusetts?

rationale.visual_potential: Similar to V01 with Harvard and MIT as neighbours.

topics.title: What if Harvard and Yale merged?

rationale.trend_strength: The Harvard–Yale rivalry is well known.
rationale.visual_potential: Two campuses fusing is visual, though less dramatic than V10.
rationale.originality: Merger of rivals is a fresh angle.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Uses the weeks 9–10 merger layout; needs a Yale kit.

topics.title: What if USC and UCLA swapped campuses?

rationale.trend_strength: Crosstown rivalry with large fan bases.
rationale.visual_potential: Both in Los Angeles, so the map move is short; relies on landmark contrast.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: Swap system; needs a USC kit.

topics.title: What if a professor time-traveled to 1890?

rationale.trend_strength: Time-travel hooks are popular in the reference channels.
rationale.visual_potential: Period costumes and a 1890s campus are visual.
rationale.originality: Very close to the reference channels' day-by-day history formats.
rationale.rendering_feasibility: No time-travel family in the renderer; should be engineering work first.
